answer: Yes. tools/plugin/cli.py update and install --repair load ownership-manifest.json and delete only owned_cache_paths (cache/derived, cache/index). A planted user-data file and user command survive byte-identical (signal a: matching pre/post tree hashes). Owned cache files are gone after the upgrade (signal b). A cache file not on the manifest survives. A missing manifest refuses rather than wiping. Rollback restores package blobs only; a wholesale-snapshot mutant drops user data and is the 11347 regression seed going red in the same run. SUCCESS:TST-0175

question_or_target: Does `update` / `install --repair` invalidate exactly the caches it owns while leaving user data untouched? PASS requires an explicit ownership manifest for cache paths; anything not on it must survive the upgrade byte-identical.

residual_unknowns.claim: platform/plugin/cache.py is absent on this Linux worktree. The live SUT for TST-0175 is tools/plugin, which implements the catalog ownership-manifest contract for update / install --repair / rollback.
